name: Benaiah
overview: Benaiah was a male Levite who held significant military leadership roles under King David. He was notably over the Cherethites and the Pelethites and served as commander of the third division of David's army. He was also recognized as the fifth among "the thirty," an elite group of David's warriors.
namesAndTitles: The name Benaiah means "y-h-v-h has built," reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges God's role in his life. This proper name is recorded in 2 Samuel 8:18.
familyAndRelationships: Benaiah was the son of Jehoiada, as explicitly stated in Scripture. He is also inferred to be the son of Ammizabad. In his role, he was responsible for executing justice by killing Adonijah, Joab, and Shimei, demonstrating his loyalty to the Davidic kingdom.
scriptureSignificance: Benaiah's importance in the biblical narrative lies in his military leadership and his role in upholding King David's authority. As commander over elite troops and one of David's mighty men, he was entrusted with critical tasks, including carrying out capital judgments against key figures who opposed the king. His service highlights the divine providence and order within David's reign.
